study.title: Effect of Electro-Acupuncture and Moxibustion on Brain Connectivity in Patients with Crohn's Disease: A Resting-State fMRI Study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial; two-arm parallel group; resting-state fMRI before and after 12-week treatment
study.randomization: Simple randomization using a random number table generated using SPSS 16.0 statistical software by a non-related individual; subjects with odd random numbers assigned to electro-acupuncture group, even random numbers to moxibustion group
study.population: CD patients from the Specialist Outpatient Department of IBD, Shanghai Research Institute of Acupuncture and Meridian, and the Endoscopy Center of Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University
study.inclusion_criteria: 18–70 years of age; education history ≥6 years; right-hand dominant; disease remission >1 year; Crohn's disease activity index (CDAI) score ≤150; CDEIS score <3; and no history of acupuncture or moxibustion treatment
study.exclusion_criteria: serum C-reactive protein >10 mg/L; erythrocyte sedimentation rate >20 mm/h; platelet level >300 × 10^9/L; presence of abdominal fistula or sinus tract; history of medical therapy with glucocorticoids, immunosuppressants, anti-TNF-α agents or other biologics, mental health medications, or opioids in the past 3 months; in a pregnant state; currently experiencing or had a history of mental/neurological disease, brain trauma, or loss of consciousness; with chronic damage or disease of the heart, liver, or kidneys; or had experienced tuberculosis, acute suppurative disease, or an infectious disease. MRI exclusion: history of abdominal surgery related to CD; claustrophobia; presence of metal inside the body; or over 50 years of age

arms.dropouts: In the electro-acupuncture group, one patient had head motion during the MRI scan, and one patient was not scanned due to a conflict of schedule. Among the 25 patients who were not scheduled for MRI scans, 12 patients were in the electro-acupuncture group (five were older than 50 years of age, three had metal implants in their body, and four had refused to receive the MRI scan)

Among the 25 patients who were not scheduled for MRI scans, 13 patients were in the moxibustion group (five were older than 50 years of age, six had metal implants in their body, and two had refused to receive the MRI scan)

interventions.stimulation_type: electro-acupuncture with mechanical needle insertion followed by electrical stimulation
interventions.laterality_exact: bilateral ST25; CV6 and CV12 are midline
interventions.needle_type_exact: acupuncture needle (Hwato, Suzhou Medical Appliance Factory)
interventions.penetration_exact: rapidly inserted through the skin, then slowly inserted an additional 20–25 mm into the subcutaneous region
interventions.manipulation_exact: After achieving a Qi sensation of acupuncture, the needles were connected to a Han's Acupoint Nerve Stimulator (HANS-100). Two electrodes of the stimulators (not divided into positive and negative charge) were connected to the left ST25 and CV6, as well as the right ST25 and CV12. The two clips did not touch each other.
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: After achieving a Qi sensation of acupuncture
interventions.needle_retention_exact: needles were left in place for 30 min
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once every other day (3 days per week) for a total of 12 weeks (36 total sessions)
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: According to our previous studies (Bao et al., 2014; Bao C. et al., 2016), four acupoints were selected for both groups

interventions.stimulation_type: herb-partitioned moxibustion; warm stimulation on acupoints
interventions.laterality_exact: bilateral ST25; CV6 and CV12 are midline
interventions.manipulation_exact: For each acupoint, two moxa-cones were burnt
interventions.session_duration_exact: not_reported explicitly for moxibustion session duration
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: According to our previous studies (Bao et al., 2014; Bao C. et al., 2016), four acupoints were selected for both groups. The warm stimulation is a key factor for the outcome of moxibustion treatment
interventions.moxibustion_composition_exact: herbal disc composed of Monkshood, Coptis chinensis, Radix aucklandiae, Carthamus tinctorius, Salvia and Angelica sinensis. Each herbal disc contained 2.8 g raw power. The powder was mixed with maltose (3 g) and made into a paste with warm water. The herbal disc was prepared to a uniform size using a mold (23 mm in diameter, 5 mm in thickness). Refined pure mugwort (size, 18 mm × 200 mm; Hanyi; Nanyang Hanyi Moxibustion Technology Development Co., Ltd.) was cut to a 16 mm height (final weight 1.8 g) for herb-partitioned moxibustion treatment.

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: After achieving a Qi sensation of acupuncture
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi was stated as a procedural requirement/milestone for electro-acupuncture; no quantitative deqi measurement instrument was reported

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: During moxibustion treatment, the abdomen of the patient was always warm. The patient was pleased and felt positive regarding the warm stimulation generated by moxibustion treatment, which increased the attention of the patient on the abdomen.
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Described narratively in the Discussion; no formal sensory measurement instrument was reported

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: echo-planar imaging sequence for resting-state fMRI; multi-echo magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MPRAGE) for T1-weighted imaging
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: in-plane resolution = 1 mm × 1 mm, slice thickness = 5 mm with no gaps and 32 slices (resting-state fMRI); slice thickness = 1.0 mm and 176 slices (T1); resampled into 3 × 3 × 3 mm3 resolution
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel of 6 mm full-width at half maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Six head motion parameters used as nuisance covariates; one patient excluded due to head motion during MRI scan
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: temporally bandpass filtered (0.01–0.1 Hz); linear trend removed
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: seed-based whole-brain rsFC analysis using bilateral hippocampus as seeds
statistical_thresholds_exact: P < 0.05, false discovery rate (FDR) corrected and the cluster size ≥48 (within-group paired t-test)
P < 0.05, FDR corrected and the cluster size ≥48 (between-group two-sample t-test)
P < 0.05 using the Bonferroni correction (Pearson's correlation between rsFC changes and CDAI scores)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: false discovery rate (FDR) corrected; Bonferroni correction for correlation analyses

additional_details.nuisance_regressors: Six head motion parameters, signals of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and signals from white matter
additional_details.seed_definition: WFU Pickatlas Tool used to define the bilateral hippocampus
additional_details.correlation_method: Pearson correlation coefficients between mean BOLD time course from seed region and all other brain voxels; converted to z values using Fisher's r-to-z transformation

extraction_notes.note: No coordinate tables are provided in the paper. All neuroimaging results are reported narratively and via figures only. Coordinates for identified brain regions (MCC, insula, precuneus, IPC, hippocampus) cannot be extracted from the text or figures. The figures show brain slices with T value color scales and some slice position labels (e.g., z=-3, z=21, z=-48, z=42, z=36, z=23, z=29, z=-31) but these appear to be MNI z-slice positions rather than peak coordinates, and no full MNI triplets are provided.

The figure labels showing numbers such as 21, -48, 42, 36, 23, 29, -31, -3 adjacent to brain slices in Figures 2 and 3 appear to be slice position values (likely MNI z-coordinate of the displayed slice) rather than cluster sizes or peak coordinates. They are not accompanied by x and y values. Extracted cluster_size_exact fields for figure-only results reflect these figure labels cautiously and should be interpreted carefully.

No sham or placebo control group was included. The Ethical Committee rejected the initial protocol to include a placebo control group. This limits causal interpretation of neural changes as specific to treatment.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events were not reported in the paper.

Deqi was only mentioned as a procedural milestone for electro-acupuncture ('after achieving a Qi sensation of acupuncture'). No quantitative deqi measurement instrument (e.g., MASS, MGQ, VAS) was used or reported.
The session duration for moxibustion is not explicitly stated in the paper. Only the number of sessions (36 over 12 weeks) and number of moxa cones per acupoint (two) are described.

Table 1 shows statistically significant differences between the two MRI groups in gender (X2 = 5.158, P = 0.023) and concomitant medication/mesalazine use (X2 = 26.947, P = 0.000). The moxibustion group had all 20 patients on mesalazine while the electro-acupuncture group had 15/18. Despite this, the paper does not discuss potential confounding of mesalazine use on neuroimaging outcomes.

The paper uses FDR correction for neuroimaging contrasts and Bonferroni correction for correlation analyses. These are applied to different types of analyses and the specific form of Bonferroni correction (number of comparisons corrected for) is not stated.

The figure caption for Figure 2C refers to 'brain regions showing less of an increase of rsFC with the left hippocampus after electro-acupuncture compared to moxibustion treatment' — this is the electro-acupuncture > moxibustion contrast. The wording 'less of an increase' is potentially confusing but the contrast direction (EA > moxa in rsFC change) is confirmed in the results text.
The paper references Supplementary Tables S1–S4 for sex-stratified clinical outcomes, but these supplementary materials are not included in the provided PDF.

No healthy control group was included in the neuroimaging analyses. The paper references prior studies showing baseline differences between CD patients and healthy volunteers but does not include HC comparisons in the current study.

The paper refers to 'anterior middle cingulate cortex (MCC)' in the results. This is a specific subregion. In Figure 2C it is labeled as 'MCC'. The precise Brodmann area or anatomical subregion boundaries are not defined.
